reviewScope: Selected proof bodies, explicit hypotheses and immediate input packages compared with the website exposition. Not an exhaustive dependency graph, complete mathematical audit, Lean build or final-theorem axiom audit. Related-input links are an explanatory dependency map; unlisted inputs remain in the source descriptions.

statusDefinitions.explained: Fully explained at the explicitly stated scope, given its named inputs. This does not rate the entire transitive proof chain.
statusDefinitions.summarized: The statement, role or main mechanism is present, but important constructions or deductions remain compressed.
statusDefinitions.missing: The argument itself is not explained in the guide. It may be named or invoked; this does not mean its Lean proof is absent.

branches.title: Arithmetic windows
branches.description: Track how exceptional twists, a compatible prime pair and finite-character averaging produce the usable window estimate.

branches.description: The integral and graded length calculations are much more developed than the construction and automorphy inputs that make them applicable.

branches.title: Local representation theory
branches.description: Distinguish the restricted local-parameter construction from its classification inputs and the weighted multiplicity bound.

branches.title: Theta integrals and test vectors
branches.description: The quantitative comparisons have explicit calculations. Constructing the required vectors and a single separating pair remains a substantial task.

branches.description: Using a finite-degree bound is a different argument from proving it. The determinant, arithmetic-volume and positivity inputs need separate explanations.

branches.title: Final assembly
branches.description: Keep the same mathematical family throughout the comparisons, fix loss exponents before epsilon, and identify where the final theorem obtains its input packages.

priorities.title: Prove the modular-family, seed and arithmetic support inputs.
priorities.why: The component-chain induction, connected-core constructions and global propagation contradiction are now expanded alongside point specialization and automorphy transfer. The remaining inputs are the ordinary modular family and seeds, the arithmetic patching support theorems behind the local transfer rules, the supplying coordinate and dimension results, and arithmetic-point classicality. The constrained deformation model also needs its own construction.

priorities.title: Finish the geometric seed and its local properties.
priorities.why: Explain how the required rank is extracted from a larger geometric representation, then why fixed-weight crystalline and Frobenius conditions survive the trace limit. An annihilating polynomial and convergent traces alone do not supply these conclusions.

priorities.title: Construct the theta vectors and the shared family.
priorities.why: Show how nonzero local vectors form a global tensor, why one selected pair separates every needed row, and how the common grid and field extension make all comparisons apply to the same family. This connects the analytic estimates to actual compatible arithmetic data.

priorities.title: Prove the finite-degree geometric estimate.
priorities.why: The current notes explain how to use the Hilbert–Samuel inequality. The next chapter should derive it from a filtration, short independent columns and a determinant, keeping the positivity and arithmetic-volume inputs explicit. Those deeper inputs are substantial projects of their own.

priorities.title: Connect the cohomology budget to every local and exceptional contribution.
priorities.why: Derive the finite exceptional-twist set from tower cohomology and explain the five prime classes in the weighted local divisibility estimate. These are the remaining arithmetic steps between the developed trace budget and the window used by Landau.

priorities.title: Derive the auxiliary-character analytic inputs.
priorities.why: The interval and prime-pair selection are explained given their estimates. Fill in the squarefree-correlation mean square, mollifier zero detection and shifted-contour tail argument; each deserves its own bounded derivation with the stated constants and ranges.
